gap: No result ChatGPT got says that on 2026-11-08 SkyFi Audio, a US restorer, had every serviced Nakamichi Dragon and CR-7A listing sold out (call for a waitlist, 'usually a 3 month lead-time' for a restored CR-7A), while the TEAC W-1200 was $599.99 and in stock at Music Direct.
standout_why: I compared against StereoNET (cited in all three chats) and Tape Lab (tapelab.live, cited). StereoNET prices the W-1200 at 'approx. USD $549' and says vintage Nakamichi and Revox decks start 'from approx. GBP £1,500', with no live listing and nothing on whether you can actually buy one. Tape Lab gives no prices at all. ChatGPT's own used-price table says it is 'not verified live listings'. Portcycling returned 403 and I could not read it. No rival shows a dated, buyable price next to whether a vintage pick can be bought at all.
decides: This backs TEAC W-1200 as the pick for someone who wants to buy a deck today. ChatGPT's top two picks (Dragon, CR-7A) could not be bought restored from the main US restorer on the read date: every listing was sold out, with a waitlist or lead time. That makes them a hunt rather than a purchase. The trade-off is real, though. The W-1200's rated wow and flutter is 0.25% W.RMS, about 9 times the CR-7A's 0.027% quoted by SkyFi. So the page should frame the vintage decks as 'better if you can find and wait for one' and keep the W-1200 as 'the best you can order today'.
